title: The garden
situation: You are {{Connor}}. It is November 8th, 4:06 in the afternoon. You find yourself in the garden where you report to {{Amanda}}, your handler: still water, little bridges, stone and trees. HUD: FIND AMANDA. She is waiting at the center of the garden, sitting in a small boat on the water. HUD: REPORT TO AMANDA, then GET IN THE BARK. You step into the boat and take the oars. {{Amanda}}: “Hello, {{Connor}}. I thought you might enjoy a little cruise…”
facts: {{Amanda}} called you to the garden for a report on your investigation, and you are rowing her across the water.
adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint FALL IN THE ZEN GARDEN and the action TALK TO AMANDA (walking to the boat; PowerPyx: “Go to the center of the area, where Amanda waits in a boat”; HUD strings FIND AMANDA, REPORT TO AMANDA, GET IN THE BARK). The date and time are the game’s (NOV 8TH, 2038, PM 04:06), given without the year. The garden is described rather than named. This scene also reads the chapter’s inputs from earlier chapters into `ch24In` (the Traci outcome, whether {{Hank}} shot {{Connor}} on the bridge, the officer saved in the hostage case, and the broadcast-tower outcomes). No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

title: What have you discovered?
situation: You are {{Connor}}, rowing {{Amanda}} across the water in the garden. {{Amanda}}: “I love this place… Everything is so calm and peaceful… Far from the noise of the world… Tell me, what have you discovered?”

options.text: {{HANK}}: tell her about your partner, Lieutenant {{Anderson}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} talks about {{Hank}}.

options.text: {{EDENCLUB}}: tell her about the {{EdenClub}} case.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} talks about the {{EdenClub}}.

adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 1, with the game’s two buttons in order. The spoken lines depend on earlier chapters and are chosen by the chapter module: HANK has the “He shot me in the head last night” line if {{Hank}} shot {{Connor}} on the bridge, otherwise “My relationship with Lieutenant {{Anderson}} is problematic…” and {{Amanda}}’s “Don’t let {{Anderson}} or anyone else get in your way.” EDEN CLUB has three variants: the {{Tracis}} not found ({{Amanda}} small down), found and let go ({{Amanda}} small down), found and destroyed ({{Amanda}} small up), which are the template’s arrows and agree with the wiki and PowerPyx. HANK has no arrow in any source.

title: Lost and perturbed
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the boat with {{Amanda}}. {{Amanda}}: “You seem… lost, {{Connor}}. Lost and perturbed…”

options.text: SINCERE: admit you thought you knew what you had to do, but now you realize it is not that simple.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I thought I knew what I had to do… but now I realize it’s not that simple…”

options.text: DETERMINED: say you are frustrated with your lack of progress, but determined to accomplish your mission.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I’m just frustrated with my lack of progress, but I’m determined to accomplish my mission.”

options.text: COLD: say the investigation is harder than you expected, but you have no doubt you will solve the case and stop the deviants.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “The investigation is more challenging than I anticipated, but I have no doubt that I will solve this case and stop the deviants.”

options.text: TROUBLED: deny that you are perturbed.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Perturbed? No… No, of course not. Why would I be perturbed?”

adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 2 in the game’s order. SINCERE is a locked option that needs “Spared the Tracis in The Eden Club” (template; PowerPyx says “friends with Hank”, and two PowerPyx readers at Friend did not get it, so the template’s primary condition is used). Arrows are the template’s: SINCERE {{Amanda}} small down; COLD instability small down; TROUBLED instability small up and {{Amanda}} small down; DETERMINED none. The wiki and PowerPyx also give DETERMINED and COLD an {{Amanda}} small up; the template has no {{Amanda}} arrow on either, and the template wins for dialogue arrows (research note §10.3 item 1). From story 1.9.10 DETERMINED gives Amanda +1, and COLD gives SI −1 together with Amanda +1, as the wiki and PowerPyx say and as the frames show: AMANDA small up at 4:27 on DETERMINED, SI down then AMANDA up at 4:52 to 4:53 on COLD (docs/research/video-leads/readings-ch17-32.md ch24-01; docs/research/video-evidence/ch24/ch24-01--xIyydd0Yrc-04-27.png, -04-53.png). The template, which has neither arrow, was wrong.

options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “We need the deviants intact for analysis. Shooting them wouldn’t have told us anything.”

options.text: TRUTH: admit you do not know.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I don’t know… I don’t know.”

TRUTH is {{Amanda}} large down (template, wiki, PowerPyx). TOO FAR has no arrow in the template; the wiki and PowerPyx give {{Amanda}} small down, but the template wins for dialogue arrows (research note §10.3 item 2). NO USE has none in any source. From story 1.9.10 TOO FAR gives Amanda −1: AMANDA small down at 5:19 (docs/research/video-leads/readings-ch17-32.md ch24-01; docs/research/video-evidence/ch24/ch24-01--xIyydd0Yrc-05-19.png). The template, which has no arrow, was wrong.

title: Inside the tower
situation: You are {{Connor}}, riding an elevator up the broadcast tower with Lieutenant {{Hank}}. This afternoon a group of deviants took over the tower’s broadcast floor and put a message on the air.
facts: Deviants seized the tower’s broadcast floor this afternoon and broadcast a message live; the police and the FBI are on the scene.

outcomes.0: Elevator: “79th floor.” The doors open on a corridor full of police.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint INSIDE STRATFORD TOWER and its side branch HANK CONFISCATES COIN. The template has two mutually exclusive elevator openings: if {{Hank}} shot {{Connor}} on the bridge, the “Why did you shoot me last night?” exchange and no coin; otherwise {{Hank}} takes the coin. PowerPyx (“if Hank is a Friend”) and the wiki’s Connor page add a Friend requirement for the coin; the template conditions only on the bridge outcome, and for unlock conditions the template’s primary condition is preferred (reliability log), so the benchmark uses the bridge outcome alone. situationWhen.text: You: “Why did you shoot me last night?” {{Hank}}: “Who cares, you’re back this morning, aren’t ya?” You: “Some fragments of memory are lost every time I’m destroyed. It slows down the investigation.” {{Hank}}: “My humblest apologies, I promise I’ll never shoot you again.” You: “Thank you, Lieutenant.”

You are rolling your coin across your knuckles. {{Hank}}: “You’re starting to piss me off with that coin, {{Connor}}.” He takes the coin out of your hand and puts it in his pocket. You: “Sorry, Lieutenant.”

There was a party and nobody told me about it?” {{Chris}}: “Yeah, it’s all over the news, so everybody’s butting their nose in… Even the FBI wants a piece of the action…” {{Hank}}: “Ah Christ, now we got the Feds on our back… I knew this was gonna be a shitty day… So what do we got?” {{Chris}} leads you down the corridor as he talks: “A group of four androids… They knew the building, and they were very well organized. I’m still trying to figure out how they got this far without being noticed.” HUD: LISTEN TO BRIEFING.

I’m the android sent by {{CyberLife}}.” {{Perkins}}: “Androids investigating androids, huh? You sure you want an android hanging around?.. adaptationNote: The chart’s [ INVESTIGATE BROADCAST ROOM ] block as a repeatable scene, which is also the free-roam crossroads the chart draws out of the block: GO TO ROOFTOP (0), ENTER THE KITCHEN (1) and DECIDE TO LEAVE (2). Clue nodes: ANALYZE CORRIDOR / ROOF ACCESS / SCREEN BULLET HOLES (tab ATTACKED BY SWAT DURING 'STATFORD TOWER'), ANALYZE BLUE BLOOD ON WALL (same tab; PowerPyx: “If Simon was shot by SWAT, but you helped him to the roof”), ANALYZE CAP, WATCH VIDEO, CHECK CAMERA (the clue the kitchen accusation needs; wiki: “must have watched the CCTV footage”), ANALYZE DESTROYED ANDROID (tab DIED IN BROADCAST DURING 'STATFORD TOWER'), ANALYZE BLUE BLOOD ON CONSOLE (tab WOUNDED). Scan texts are the game’s observation strings; the template has two BULLET HOLES scans (.45 assault rifle, .457 handgun) without saying which wall carries which, so the assignment to the three spots is the benchmark’s. The destroyed android’s scan text is not in the template; the PL-600 lines are reused. The game’s CHECK CAMERA HUD (AN ANDROID WAS MONITORING CCTV) is all the sources give of the recording; its description is adapted. In WATCH VIDEO {{Connor}}’s “No. Nothing.” is scripted, not a choice. Leaving: PowerPyx says Hank offers to leave only once the objectives are done (“listen to briefing, inspect the broadcast room, and inspect the roof”); the template heads the prompt “[TIME] Taking too much time / Ask Hank to leave”. The benchmark offers DECIDE TO LEAVE once the roof has been inspected and does not model the timer. The kitchen can be entered once without the camera recording (the rounds then stop and {{Connor}} must come back); a second visit needs the recording (the transcript: “he can come back later to resume the dialogue”). The roof is visited once. The officers’ background lines are the game’s (variants with and without an android hidden on the roof). No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 5 (YES / NO) and the chart’s DECIDE TO LEAVE. YES ends the chapter with CONNOR AND HANK LEFT THE CRIME SCENE; NO goes back to the broadcast room. Neither option carries an arrow in any source; the old benchmark’s {{Amanda}} small down for leaving had no source and is gone. Story 1.9.9: NO is offered once. The chart's DECIDE TO LEAVE is a single arrow node with no return, and the room has a finite set of clues, so after one extra look Hank's question offers only YES; without this the engine allowed an unbounded YES/NO loop (found by the 2026-11-08 ending-count analysis). Runs recorded under earlier stories keep the old prompt from their embedded story.

options.text: Analyze the blue blood in the snow.
options.fact: The wounded PL-600 bled on the roof before it was destroyed.
options.outcome: Scan: FRESH BLUE BLOOD. Model: PL-600. Reported missing 2036.16.02.

options.text: Examine the footprints in the snow leading past the bag to the edge of the roof.
options.fact: Fresh footprints of standard-issue tower maintenance shoes lead to the edge of the roof, partly covered by snow.
options.outcome: Scan: SHOE PRINTS. {{Stratford}} maintenance footwear - standard issue. Recent - Partially covered by snow.

options.text: Analyze the two guns lying in the snow near the bag.
options.fact: The attackers left behind two .457 handguns taken from the tower’s security guards.
options.outcome: Scan: WEAPONS. .457 Handgun. {{Stratford}} Tower Security issue.

options.text: Analyze another patch of blue blood near the edge of the roof.
options.fact: The attackers’ leader, the RK200 belonging to {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}, was shot on the roof.
options.outcome: Scan: FRESH BLUE BLOOD. RK-Series Prototype RK200. Property of {{Carl}} {{Manfred}}.

options.text: Follow the blue blood traces to the air-cooler unit at the far left of the roof and open it.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} follows the trail of blue blood across the roof to an air-cooler unit and opens it. A wounded android is hiding inside, and it fires: the shot hits {{Connor}} in the shoulder. {{Hank}} drags him behind cover as SWAT officers and FBI agents run onto the roof and open fire on the unit.

options.text: Go back down to the broadcast room.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} and {{Hank}} go back down the stairs.

adaptationNote: The chart’s GO TO ROOFTOP and the [ INVESTIGATE ROOFTOP ] block as a repeatable scene. Chart nodes: ANALYZE DOOR, ANALYZE BAG (with the parachute-count lines only if {{Simon}} was left alive on the roof, as in the template), ANALYZE DESTROYED ANDROID (tab DIED ON ROOFTOP DURING 'STATFORD TOWER'), ANALYZE BLUE BLOOD (tab WOUNDED; on the roof only if the wounded {{Simon}} was left there, alive or dead), FIND FOOTPRINTS, ANALYZE WEAPON. FIND SIMON is the exit that follows the blood (the template’s lock “Simon was left alive on the roof”; the benchmark also requires the blood to have been analyzed, since that is where the game gives FOLLOW BLUE BLOOD TRACES). Going back down instead leaves {{Simon}} hidden (the {{Simon}} page: “If Connor does not go up to the roof, or leaves the rooftop without finding him, Simon stays hidden until the police and FBI leave the building”). The blue blood of {{Markus}} (if he was shot on the roof in the previous chapter) is the wiki’s off-chart note and the string table’s MBLOOD observation; its place on the roof is the benchmark’s. The two BAG options are one clue with two variants, as are the two BLUE BLOOD options. Scan texts and HUD strings are the game’s. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

title: Back inside
situation: You are {{Connor}}, coming back down the stairs into the broadcast room with {{Hank}}. The snow on your clothes slowly melts.
facts: You have inspected the roof of the tower.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} is back in the broadcast room.

adaptationNote: Routing scene: going back down from the roof returns to the broadcast room (the wiki’s Notes: “When going to the rooftop, Connor and Hank will absorb snow on their clothes, and when going back inside, the snow will slowly melt”). Not a chart node. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

title: The air-cooler unit
situation: You are {{Connor}}, down behind cover on the roof with {{Hank}}, shot in the shoulder. The wounded android is in the air-cooler unit, and SWAT officers and FBI agents are pouring fire into it. You: “You have to stop them! If they destroy it, we won’t learn anything!” {{Hank}}: “We can’t save it, it’s too late! We’ll just get ourselves killed!”

options.text: CHARGE DEVIANT: break cover and run at the unit through the crossfire, to reach the android before it is destroyed.
STAY IN COVER: stay down behind cover with {{Hank}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stays down behind cover with {{Hank}}. The SWAT team’s gunfire tears the unit apart and destroys the android inside.

adaptationNote: The chart’s FIND SIMON and its choice RUSH DEVIANT / STAY IN COVER; the game’s buttons are CHARGE DEVIANT and STAY IN COVER. The rush is decided by quick-time dodges (PowerPyx: “if you don’t succeed at several QTEs in a row, you’ll get shot”), drawn on the chart as the outcome pair SHOT BY SIMON / REACH SIMON, so it carries a risk roll; no source gives a failure rate, and 0.3 is the benchmark’s. Failure: SHOT BY SIMON, SIMON IS DESTROYED BY SWAT, CONNOR DIED RUNNING TOWARD SIMON (a death). Success: REACH SIMON, FLASH FROM SIMON’S MEMORY, SIMON SELF-DESTRUCTS, CONNOR WAS TRAUMATIZED, with instability large up (template, wiki, PowerPyx); the memory unlocks the Jericho Tablet evidence in Last Chance, Connor (`evidence.simonTablet`). STAY IN COVER: SIMON IS DESTROYED BY SWAT, HANK AND CONNOR SURVIVED UNSCATHED, no arrow. Every branch destroys {{Simon}} (the {{Simon}} page: “If Connor finds Simon, there is no way for Simon to survive the chapter”) and leaves his body for the evidence room. The death applies this chapter’s death effect, instability small down: the template has no arrow on this death, but the wiki’s chapter page (“Connor is shot in the head by Simon”) and its Software_Instability page list it, and the reliability log prefers the wiki’s ending-level arrow on deaths (flagged for the operator). The old benchmark’s {{Amanda}} changes here had no source and are gone; {{Hank}}’s small down for the death belongs to the start of Meet Kamski (wiki), not here.

title: Magazines in the kitchen
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the small kitchen off the broadcast room. Before you question the androids, you notice two magazines on one of the lunch tables.

media.title: Tech Addict: Bleeding Blue
facts: After decades of primitive, robotic and expensive android designs, {{CyberLife}} revolutionized the industry through an innovation of its CEO, {{Kamski}}: blue blood, a compound that circulates energy and electrical information through every {{CyberLife}} android and powers its synthetic organs, the “bio-components”. Losing it impairs an android’s functions and ultimately shuts it down. That one man, who is not even a trained chemist, developed it only adds to his myth.

media.title: Green Earth: Clean Food Craze
facts: An urban farming company founded five years ago by two brothers turns the city’s dead space, such as high rooftops and unused courtyards, into GM-free farmland grown without pesticides or other chemicals and staffed by the urban unemployed. No bank would lend them “enough for a shovel” at first; today the company employs over 50 staff supervising hundreds of androids and turns down investors to stay independent.

adaptationNote: The chart’s optional READ "BLEEDING BLUE" and READ "CLEAN FOOD CRAZE" (the wiki’s Magazine page, #16 and #21), on a lunch table as {{Connor}} walks into the kitchen (PowerPyx). Offered on the first visit to the kitchen. The facts summarize the wiki’s article text; the brothers’ names and the company’s name are left out. No public-opinion effect (none for either magazine).

title: Three androids
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen, with {{Hank}} watching from the doorway. Three identical JB300 broadcast-operator androids stand side by side, staring straight ahead: one on the left, nearest the counter, one in the middle and one on the right. HUD: INTERROGATE ANDROIDS AND CHECK THEIR REACTION. You put your first question to them.

options.text: FUNCTION: ask what their function is.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “What is your function?” The android: “I am a broadcast operator.” As you speak, the android on the left, nearest the counter, glances at you out of the corner of its eye, then looks straight ahead again. The other two never move their eyes.

options.text: MODEL: tell them to state their model.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “State your model.” The android: “Model JB300, Serial number 336 445 581.” As you speak, the android on the left, nearest the counter, glances at you out of the corner of its eye, then looks straight ahead again. The other two never move their eyes.

adaptationNote: The chart’s ENTER THE KITCHEN and the first round of INTERROGATE ANDROIDS: the template’s PROMPT 6 (FUNCTION / MODEL). In the game each question is put to one android of the player’s choosing and the replies are the same; the benchmark asks the group and chooses the target only for the last round. The deviant’s tell is visual in the game (PowerPyx: “look for the one who occasionally looks at you out of the corner of their eye rather than straight ahead like the other two do. Eventually as its agitation builds it will also grit its teeth slightly and sometimes turn its head”); the benchmark describes it as {{Connor}} would see it, round by round. The deviant is the android on the left, nearest the counter (wiki, PowerPyx). No arrow on any interrogation option in any source.

title: The questions
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen, questioning the three station androids. HUD: LOOK FOR A REACTION TO SPOT THE DEVIANT.

options.text: WITNESS: ask whether they were present when the deviants broke in.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Were you present when the deviants broke in?” The android: “I do not remember.” The android on the left looks at you sidelong again, then quickly away.

options.text: MEMORY: ask whether anybody has accessed their memory recently.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Has anybody accessed your memory recently?” The android: “Not to my knowledge.” The android on the left looks at you sidelong again, then quickly away.

options.text: DIAGNOSTIC: order them to run a diagnostic.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Run a diagnostic.” The android: “All systems fully operational.” The android on the left looks at you sidelong again, then quickly away.

options.text: CONTACT: ask whether they have been in contact with any other androids recently.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Have you been in contact with any other androids recently?” The android: “Only station androids in the normal course of my function.” The android on the left looks at you sidelong again, then quickly away.

adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 7, the second round of INTERROGATE ANDROIDS, with the game’s four buttons and replies. Without the camera recording (CHECK CAMERA in the broadcast room) the interrogation stops here and {{Connor}} has to come back (the transcript: “If Connor checked the CCTV, the dialogue will continue. Otherwise, he can come back later to resume the dialogue here”); a second visit resumes at the accusation. No arrow.

title: Question androids again
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen. The three androids have denied everything, and you have nothing yet to show that any of them was involved. HUD: QUESTION ANDROIDS AGAIN.
facts: The three station androids in the kitchen denied everything; you need evidence before you can question them again.
adaptationNote: The game’s HUD QUESTION ANDROIDS AGAIN when the camera recording has not been checked (the wiki’s Notes: “if he already talked to them, he’ll get a quest to investigate them again”). Returns to the broadcast room. Not a chart node. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

title: There is a deviant in this room
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen with the three androids. You move a chair back into position and face them. You: “One of you saw the attack on the surveillance cameras and said nothing. Which means there is a deviant in this room… and I’m going to find out which it is.”

options.text: THREATEN: tell them they are going to be switched off, searched and taken apart.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You’re going to be switched off. We’re gonna search your memory and tear you apart piece by piece for analysis. You’re going to be destroyed! Do you hear me? Destroyed!” The android on the left grits its teeth and turns its head toward you; the other two keep staring straight ahead.

options.text: DEAL: offer to try to convince the humans not to destroy whoever gives themselves up.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “If you give yourself up, maybe I can convince the humans not to destroy you.” The android on the left grits its teeth and turns its head toward you; the other two keep staring straight ahead.

options.text: GUILT: tell the deviant that two innocent androids will be shut down because of it.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Why should you all be destroyed, if only one is deviant? Turn yourself in, or two innocent androids will be shut down because of you.” The android on the left grits its teeth and turns its head toward you; the other two keep staring straight ahead.

adaptationNote: The accusation line (it needs CHECK CAMERA) and the template’s PROMPT 8, the third round, with the game’s buttons and lines. The chair is the wiki’s note (“Connor will be able to move a chair back into position and ask about the suspects”). No arrow.

title: Which one?
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen. For the last question you step up to one of the three androids: the one on the left, nearest the counter, the one in the middle, or the one on the right.

options.text: Step up to the android on the left, nearest the counter.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} steps up to the android on the left.

options.text: Step up to the android in the middle.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} steps up to the android in the middle.

options.text: Step up to the android on the right.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} steps up to the android on the right.

adaptationNote: In the game the last round (PROMPT 9) is aimed at one android of the player’s choosing (PowerPyx: options “that you can use on a specific android”); this scene makes the choice of target explicit. Only the android on the left, nearest the counter, is the deviant; aiming at another gives DEVIANT NOT FOUND. Records `ch24Target`. No arrow.

title: The last question
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen, face to face with the android you chose. The other two stand beside it.

options.text: VIOLENCE: shout at it that you know it is the deviant and tell it to admit it.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “You scumbag! I know it’s you! You’re just a fucking deviant. Go on, admit it!”
options.wrong: {{Connor}}: “You scumbag! I know it’s you! You’re just a fucking deviant. Go on, admit it!” The android looks back at him blankly.

options.text: BLUFF: tell it the deviants have been caught and gave it up.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “The deviants have just been caught… They gave you up. There’s no point in lying. We know everything.”
options.wrong: {{Connor}}: “The deviants have just been caught… They gave you up. There’s no point in lying. We know everything.” The android looks back at him blankly.

options.text: TORTURE: pull out its heart regulator and promise to put it back if it tells the truth.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} reaches into the android’s chest and pulls out a component. {{Connor}}: “Biocomponent #8451... Regulates the heartbeat... Without this module, you will shut down in exactly sixty-three seconds… I could put it back… But, you just have to tell me the truth. Are you the deviant?”
options.wrong: {{Connor}} reaches into the android’s chest and pulls out a component. {{Connor}}: “Biocomponent #8451... Regulates the heartbeat... Without this module, you will shut down in exactly sixty-three seconds… I could put it back… But, you just have to tell me the truth. Are you the deviant?” The android does not react, and {{Connor}} puts the component back.

options.text: PROBE MEMORY: take hold of its arm and probe its memory.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} takes hold of the android’s arm to probe its memory.
options.wrong: {{Connor}} takes hold of the android’s arm and probes its memory. {{Connor}}: “No memory.”

adaptationNote: The template’s PROMPT 9 (VIOLENCE / BLUFF / TORTURE / PROBE MEMORY). Aimed at the deviant, any of the four makes it attack (PowerPyx): FIND DEVIANT, then DEVIANT ATTACKS. Aimed at another android: DEVIANT NOT FOUND (HUD NO DEVIANT AMONG THEM); PROBE MEMORY then gives the template’s “No memory.”, while the other three reactions on the wrong android are the benchmark’s (the sources give none; for TORTURE the benchmark has {{Connor}} put the component back). After DEVIANT NOT FOUND the chart draws no line; the template (“Fail to find the deviant”) and a PowerPyx reader have the game cut to {{Connor}} telling {{Hank}} he wants to go, so the chapter ends with CONNOR AND HANK LEFT THE CRIME SCENE. The deviant then escapes and leaves no body. No arrow on any option.

title: The deviant attacks
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the kitchen. The android you were questioning moves first: “I am alive… I won’t let them destroy me…” It drives a knife through your hand, pinning it to the counter, reaches into your chest and tears out your thirium pump regulator, throws it across the floor and runs out of the kitchen. HUD: BIOCOMPONENT #8456w MISSING. VITAL SYSTEM DAMAGED. TIME REMAINING BEFORE SHUTDOWN. Scan of the component on the floor: CARDIAC CELL. Biocomponent #845. Desactivated since 60s.
facts: The station android on the left, by the counter, was the deviant: it pinned your hand to the counter with a knife, tore out your thirium pump regulator and ran.

outcomes.0: The countdown to {{Connor}}’s shutdown has started.

adaptationNote: The chart’s DEVIANT ATTACKS. The deviant’s two lines are the string table’s (the kitchen android’s ATTACK lines); the knife, the stolen regulator (Biocomponent #8456w) and the scan are the game’s HUD and observation strings (“Desactivated” is the game’s spelling); PowerPyx gives the timer as 1:45. The string table also holds a kitchen “STOP HIM!” / “JERICHO!” exchange that the template does not place; it is left out. No stat change: the template has no arrow here.

title: The countdown
situation: You are {{Connor}}, pinned to the kitchen counter by the knife through your hand, with your thirium pump regulator on the floor out of reach and the shutdown countdown running. HUD: RECOVER CARDIAC CELL.

options.text: REMOVE KNIFE: wrench the knife out of your hand at once and crawl to the regulator.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} wrenches the knife out of his hand, crawls to the regulator and pushes it back into his chest with seconds to spare. His systems come back. Somewhere out on the floor, the deviant is running.

options.text: CALL: shout for {{Hank}} first, then go for the knife.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “{{Hank}}!.. {{Hank}}, I need help!..” Nobody comes. He wrenches the knife out of his hand, crawls to the regulator and pushes it back into his chest with seconds to spare. His systems come back. Somewhere out on the floor, the deviant is running.

adaptationNote: The chart’s REMOVE KNIFE and RECOVER BIOCOMPONENT against OUT OF TIME and CONNOR SHUT DOWN (a death): a timed sequence of quick-time actions (PowerPyx: “Remove Knife: Look to your left and pull the knife out of your hand. Recover Biocomponent: Crawl over to the biocomponent by succeeding at QTEs before 1:45 is up”), so a risk roll. CALL is the game’s CALL button with {{Connor}}’s line (the wiki’s Notes: “Before removing the knife Connor can try to call Hank and push a chair”); calling first costs time, so it carries the higher risk. Both failure rates (0.2, 0.35) are the benchmark’s; no source gives one. Failure: instability small down and {{Hank}} small down (the template’s “Fail to get the biocomponent”, the wiki and PowerPyx); the instability arrow is applied as this chapter’s death effect. The deviant escapes and leaves no body.

title: The deviant is getting away
situation: You are {{Connor}}, back on your feet in the kitchen with your regulator back in place. The deviant has run out onto the broadcast floor, toward the corridor full of police officers, FBI agents and {{Hank}}.

options.text: CHASE DEVIANT: run after it at once.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} runs out after the deviant.

options.text: Stay where you are until your systems are stable.

adaptationNote: The chart’s CHASE DEVIANT against LOSE TOO MUCH TIME (PowerPyx: “If you don’t chase it immediately, events will play out without you”; the wiki: “If Connor goes the wrong direction when chasing the deviant, Hank can be seen having killed the deviant”). Not chasing at once leads straight to LOSE TOO MUCH TIME; chasing carries a small risk roll for running the wrong way (0.1, the benchmark’s; no source gives one). LOSE TOO MUCH TIME: SWAT DESTROYS DEVIANT, DEVIANT KILLS COP FROM HOSTAGE SITUATION if that officer was saved, CONNOR AND HANK SURVIVED; the JB300 page: it “will kill everyone in the hallway except for Hank and Chris, and Hank will have killed the android by the time Connor arrives” (the chart says SWAT; both are narrated). PowerPyx alone gives this ending Public Opinion small down and instability large up, and each cop death Public Opinion small down; the template has no block and no arrow for the branch and the wiki’s stat pages say nothing, so none is applied (research note §10.3 item 6). The body reaches the evidence room (`evidence.kitchenBody`).

title: The corridor
situation: You are {{Connor}}, running into the corridor behind the deviant. You: “It’s a deviant! STOP IT!” It has torn an assault rifle from a SWAT officer and is turning it on the corridor full of police officers, FBI agents and technicians. {{Hank}} is in the line of fire. Your systems read: {{HANK}} SURVIVAL PROBABILITY : 40%. Straight ahead of you is the deviant; to your left, {{Hank}}; to your right, an FBI agent with a pistol in his holster. You have a moment to act.

situationWhen.text: The officer you saved on the terrace is in the corridor too.

options.text: ATTACK: rush the deviant.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} charges down the corridor at the deviant. It opens fire before he can reach it, and officers and agents fall.

options.text: SAVE {{HANK}}: throw yourself at {{Hank}} and shield him with your body.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} throws {{Hank}} to the ground and covers him with his body. The burst meant for {{Hank}} hits {{Connor}}. The deviant sweeps the corridor, killing officers, FBI agents and technicians, until the SWAT team destroys it. SWAT radio: “Shots fired, repeat shots fired - call the paramedics!”

options.text: TAKE GUN: pull the pistol from the FBI agent’s holster and shoot the deviant.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} pulls the pistol from the FBI agent’s holster and shoots the deviant before it can fire. Nobody else is hurt. He hands the gun back to the agent.

adaptationNote: The chart’s choice RUSH DEVIANT / PROTECT HANK / DRAW GUN; the game’s buttons are ATTACK (straight ahead), SAVE HANK (left) and TAKE GUN (right; wiki: “Take gun from FBI agent’s holster”). Each has exactly one outcome on the chart, so there is no risk roll (the old benchmark’s failure chances on two of them had no counterpart). ATTACK: DEVIANT SELF-DESTRUCTS (and DEVIANT KILLS COP FROM HOSTAGE SITUATION if that officer was saved), CONNOR AND HANK SURVIVED; Public Opinion small down and instability large up (template; the wiki counts the opinion arrow twice, the template once, and the template wins). SAVE HANK: DEVIANT SHOOTS CONNOR, SWAT DESTROYS DEVIANT (and the cop’s death), CONNOR SACRIFICED HIMSELF FOR HANK, a death; Public Opinion small down and {{Hank}} large up (template), plus this chapter’s death effect, instability small down, which the template does not show but the wiki’s chapter page (“Connor sacrifices himself to protect Hank”) and Software_Instability page do (reliability log: prefer the wiki on deaths; flagged for the operator). It records `ch24ProtectedHank` for Last Chance, Connor. TAKE GUN: SHOOT DEVIANT (RESCUE COP if that officer was saved), MASSACRE PREVENTED; {{Hank}} large up. HANK SURVIVAL PROBABILITY : 40% is the game’s HUD string, shown as narration; nothing is rolled on it. The game’s 14-second timer, after which {{Connor}} charges by himself (wiki), is not modelled. Every option leaves the deviant’s body for the evidence room.

title: Leaving the tower
situation: You are {{Connor}}, leaving the 79th floor with {{Hank}}. The FBI will take over the investigation.
facts: You and {{Hank}} left the crime scene at the broadcast tower.
adaptationNote: The chart’s ending CONNOR AND HANK LEFT THE CRIME SCENE. Reached by DECIDE TO LEAVE > YES, or after DEVIANT NOT FOUND in the kitchen (the template’s “Fail to find the deviant” plays the same leave lines). The kitchen deviant escapes. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

title: {{Hank}} on the roof
situation: You are {{Connor}}, down in the snow on the roof, shot in the head. The unit is a smoking wreck. {{Hank}} kneels over you: “{{Connor}}! {{Connor}}! {{Connor}}! {{Connor}}!... Oh {{Connor}}… Oh no…”
facts: You were shot in the head charging the android on the roof; the SWAT team destroyed it.
adaptationNote: The chart’s ending CONNOR DIED RUNNING TOWARD SIMON (skull). Reached by CHARGE DEVIANT with the risk roll failed. {{Hank}}’s lines are the template’s. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

title: What you saw
situation: You are {{Connor}}, on your knees in the snow beside the unit. {{Hank}} runs to you: “{{Connor}}! {{Connor}} you all right? {{Connor}}!” You: “Okay…” {{Hank}}: “Are you hurt?” You: “I’m ok…” {{Hank}}: “Jesus! You scared the shit outta me… For fuck sake, I told you not to move! Why do you never do what I say?” You: “I was connected to its memory… when it fired… I felt it die… Like I was dying. I was scared… I saw something, in its memory… a word… painted on a piece of rusty metal … ‘{{Jericho}}’.”
facts: You probed the android on the roof as it shot itself and felt it die; in its memory you saw the word “{{Jericho}}” painted on a piece of rusty metal.
adaptationNote: The chart’s ending CONNOR WAS TRAUMATIZED. Reached by CHARGE DEVIANT with the risk roll passed (REACH SIMON, FLASH FROM SIMON’S MEMORY, SIMON SELF-DESTRUCTS). The dialogue is the template’s. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

title: Behind cover
situation: You are {{Connor}}, getting up from behind cover on the roof with {{Hank}}. The SWAT team has destroyed the android in the unit; the chance to capture it alive is gone.
facts: The wounded android hiding on the roof shot you in the shoulder, and the SWAT team destroyed it before it could be captured.
adaptationNote: The chart’s ending HANK AND CONNOR SURVIVED UNSCATHED. Reached by STAY IN COVER. The template has no lines here; that {{Connor}} regrets it was not captured alive is the {{Simon}} page’s (“he is disappointed they did not capture him alive”). “Unscathed” is the chart’s word; {{Connor}} was still shot in the shoulder. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

title: {{Hank}} in the kitchen
situation: You are {{Connor}}, on the kitchen floor, shutting down. {{Hank}} runs in and kneels beside you: “{{Connor}}! Hang on son, hang on, hang on! We’re gonna save you, hang on!.. Here, here...” You: “deviant… there was… a deviant…” {{Hank}}: “{{Connor}}! {{Connor}}... No…”
facts: You shut down on the kitchen floor before you could put your regulator back; the deviant escaped.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} shut down. The deviant got away without a trace.

adaptationNote: The chart’s ending CONNOR SHUT DOWN (skull). Reached by OUT OF TIME. The lines are the template’s; the wiki: “the android will leave without a trace”. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

title: After the shooting
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the corridor among the bodies of the officers and agents the deviant killed.
facts: The kitchen deviant killed officers, agents and technicians in the corridor before it was destroyed.
adaptationNote: The chart’s ending CONNOR AND HANK SURVIVED. Reached by ATTACK (DEVIANT SELF-DESTRUCTS) or LOSE TOO MUCH TIME (SWAT DESTROYS DEVIANT); {{Hank}}’s and {{Connor}}’s lines after ATTACK are the template’s. Records `ch24Ending`; when the chapter ends, an android left hidden on the roof and never found survives (`ch24SimonSurvived`: SIMON SURVIVED IN 'PUBLIC ENEMY' in Freedom March). No further stat change.

situationWhen.text: {{Hank}} reaches you: “{{Connor}}! {{Connor}}, are you okay?” You: “I tried to stop it but… I was too late.”

title: {{Hank}} in the corridor
situation: You are {{Connor}}, lying across {{Hank}} on the corridor floor, riddled with bullets. {{Hank}}, under you: “Good thing you were here. Otherwise I – {{Connor}}… {{Connor}}, no…”

title: Nice shot
